title: Inheritance process — step by step, with deadlines

sections.title: 1. The five clocks that decide the money
sections.intro: Almost every expensive mistake in a California inheritance is a missed deadline, not a wrong calculation. These are the deadlines that apply to Property A.

rows.item: Move in (or don't) — Prop 19 principal-residence test
rows.note: This is the decision deadline for live-vs-rent. There is no extension.

rows.item: Claim the homeowners' exemption
rows.note: Required for the Prop 19 exclusion. File by February 15 of the year you want the exemption to apply in full.

rows.item: Claim the parent-child exclusion
rows.value: Within 3 years of the transfer, or before sale (BOE-19-P)
rows.note: Filing after 1 year but within 3 years can still work if the exemption and residency tests were met.

rows.item: Federal estate tax return
rows.note: Only if the gross estate plus taxable gifts exceeds the exclusion.

rows.item: Property tax installments
rows.note: A 10% penalty applies immediately — this is the most common avoidable cost after a death.

rows.item: Trustee's notification to beneficiaries and heirs
rows.value: Required when the revocable trust becomes irrevocable
rows.note: Starts the contest period. The statute's practical deadline is commonly stated as 60 days — that specific number is secondary, not read from the statute here.

sections.title: 2. Before the death (2026–2039) — what to fix while there is still time

rows.item: Confirm Property A is the parents' principal residence on the assessor's record
rows.value: Homeowners' exemption present on the tax bill
rows.note: Prop 19 only works for the parent's principal residence. If the exemption is not on the bill, the full $3.1M reassessment applies.

rows.item: Confirm the trust is funded
rows.value: Deed shows the trustee as record owner
rows.note: A trust that owns nothing avoids nothing. Check the recorded deed, not the binder.

rows.item: Confirm what the trust does to the step-up
rows.value: Property must be included in the grantor's gross estate
rows.note: An irrevocable, non-includible trust produces carry-over basis. Worth ≈$945,000 in avoided capital gains on Property A. Ask the estate attorney for written confirmation — F-14.

rows.item: Record the capital-improvement history
rows.note: Needed for the Form 706 value and for any later basis question.

rows.item: Photograph the original solar interconnection date
rows.value: NEM legacy term (20 years) is tied to the system
rows.note: A pre-2023 system loses retail-rate net metering by 2043 at the latest.

rows.item: Get a replacement-cost estimate and a home inspection
rows.note: Drives insurance and maintenance. Owner has not supplied either — F-07.

rows.item: Confirm flood / fire hazard zone status
rows.note: Determines whether a FAIR Plan wrap is needed. Not supplied — F-06.

rows.item: Decide the family policy now: who lives there, who sells, who rents
rows.note: The 12-month clock after death is the worst time to negotiate this.

rows.item: 1. Obtain certified death certificates
rows.note: Banks, title, insurers and the assessor each want one.

rows.item: 2. Locate the original trust and any amendments; successor trustee accepts
rows.note: If there is a will that names the trust, the original will is lodged with the court.

rows.item: 3. Secure the property and notify the insurer
rows.note: Vacant houses lose coverage quickly; a landlord or vacant-property endorsement is usually required.

rows.item: 4. Serve the trustee's notification
rows.note: To each beneficiary and each heir of the deceased settlor.

rows.item: 5. Obtain a trust EIN
rows.note: Required to open accounts and to file Form 1041 / CA Form 541.

rows.item: 6. Order a date-of-death appraisal
rows.value: As of the date of death
rows.note: This is the number that sets both the step-up basis and, for Property A, the Prop 19 market value. One appraisal serves both.

rows.item: 7. Record the transfer to the beneficiaries (trustee's deed)
rows.note: Recording triggers the assessor's change-of-ownership review.

rows.item: 8. Tell the county assessor
rows.value: Preliminary change of ownership report with the deed
rows.note: Santa Clara County Assessor handles the Prop 19 claim and the new base year value.

rows.item: 9. File BOE-266 (homeowners' exemption)
rows.note: Mandatory for the exclusion — do this even if the long-term plan is to sell.

rows.item: 10. File BOE-19-P (parent-child exclusion)
rows.note: Do not wait to see whether the assessor notices.

rows.item: 11. Notify the mortgage servicer if there is a loan
rows.note: Federal law restricts enforcement of due-on-sale clauses on a transfer by inheritance, but the servicer must still be told and the loan assumed formally. No loan data supplied — F-15.

rows.item: 12. Re-title insurance for the actual use
rows.note: Claims get denied when the policy use does not match reality.

rows.item: 13. Set up the property tax calendar
rows.note: Expect a supplemental bill for the difference between the old and new assessed values.

rows.item: 14. File Form 706 if required
rows.note: Also the moment to make the portability election.

rows.item: 15. Final income tax returns
rows.note: Trust rental income is reported while the trust holds the property.

rows.item: 16. Sell with a stepped-up basis, if that is the decision
rows.value: No capital gain on the date-of-death value
rows.note: Selling in the year of death is the cleanest tax outcome in the whole plan.
